## Code-conventions review: `191d616e1...HEAD` (feature-flag override editor)

I generated the checklist from `docs/engineering/sources/rules.json` and went through all 90 rules against the 28 changed files. You asked me not to create files, so the checklist went to my scratchpad instead of `docs/engineering/`. I changed no tracked files, ran no tests or installs, and posted nothing. I didn't need to look up the review history behind any rule.

**Rules that applied:** FEAT-01, FEAT-02, FEAT-03, CODE-02, CODE-04, TEST-01, TEST-02, TEST-03, TEST-05, WEB-04, RTK-02, DATA-02, SEC-01, UI-01, API-01, UX-03.

### Findings

| # | Rule | Where | Finding |
|---|------|-------|---------|
| 1 | **FEAT-03** / web `project-structure.md` ("Inside a feature, import siblings via relative paths") | `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/components/FeatureFlagEditor.tsx:7`, `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/components/FeatureFlagRow.tsx:10`, `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/hooks/useFeatureFlagEditorData.ts:7` | Code inside `features/feature-flags` imports its own store through the absolute path `@/features/feature-flags/store`. The same files use relative imports for everything else (`../hooks/...`, `./FeatureFlagSection`). Use `../store` so the whole feature follows one style. |
| 2 | **CODE-02** (example `code-02-move-heavy-tailwind-class-strings-into-css-modules`) | `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/components/FeatureFlagRow.tsx:46`, `:19`; `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/components/FeatureFlagSection.tsx:27` | Several long Tailwind strings with custom values: a six-part `before:` accent bar (`before:w-[3px] ... before:content-['']`), an exported `GRID` constant with custom `grid-cols-[minmax(...)...]` shared between two files, and a header with `text-[10.5px] ... [&>:last-child]:text-right`. The documented rule is to move these into a named class in a CSS module (e.g. `.overriddenRow`, `.grid`). That also replaces the exported string constant. |
| 3 | **TEST-05** ("Use `Builder.new<T>().with({...})` data for unit tests") | `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/hooks/useFeatureFlagEditorData.test.tsx:9`; `apps/web/src/hooks/useChains.test.ts:9`, `:44`, `:62` | Test chains are hand-built with `({ chainId, features }) as unknown as Chain`. The repo already has `chainBuilder` in `apps/web/src/tests/builders/chains.ts`, which gives a fully typed chain with randomised fields: `chainBuilder().with({ chainId, features }).build()`. Using it would drop the double cast, which also works against the "never use `any`"-style type bypassing in `AGENTS.md`. |
| 4 | **Web feature structure** (`project-structure.md`: "always: `components/<Component>/index.tsx`") | `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/components/FeatureFlagEditor.tsx`, `FeatureFlagRow.tsx`, `FeatureFlagSection.tsx` | The components are flat files under `components/`. The documented layout is one folder per component with `index.tsx` and the test and story next to it. The repo follows this in 232 places against 16 flat files. |
| 5 | **FEAT-02** / `project-structure.md` ("Avoid copying: any feature that re-exports internal components or services through its barrel") | `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/index.ts:1` | The barrel exports only the implementation component `FeatureFlagEditor`. There is no `feature.ts` or `createFeatureHandle`. This looks deliberate: `pages/feature-flags.tsx` loads the barrel through a dynamic import behind the production check, so production builds can drop the editor. Other code reaches the slice via `@/features/<x>/store`, which matches existing features (`hypernative`, `gtf`). **Judgment call:** add a one-line note in the PR description explaining the deviation, so nobody copies this shape for normal features. |
| 6 | **RTK-02** + `AGENTS.md` pitfall #6 ("Always handle loading, error, and empty states") | `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/hooks/useFeatureFlagEditorData.ts:32`, `:26`; `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/components/FeatureFlagSection.tsx:15` | The hook reads only `data` from `useGetChainsConfigV2Query` and ignores `isLoading` and `error`. While chains load, or if the request fails, `chains` is `[]`. Every row then shows an "Off" badge and a `false` config value, which looks like real data. Separately, when a search matches nothing, both sections return `null` and the page is blank below the toolbar, with no "no matching flags" message. |

### Checked and fine

- **WEB-04:** the Developer group goes through the same `resolveItem` and `getLink`, so the Space ID in the URL is kept (and a test covers it).
- **TEST-03:** the pure `applyFeatureOverrides` is tested separately from the hooks.
- **TEST-01:** the bundle-exclusion test has a guard so it can't pass on empty output.
- **TEST-02:** the production, empty and `null` branches of the Developer group are each tested.
- **UI-01:** colours use theme tokens such as `success-subtle` and `success-strong`.
- **SEC-01:** `Object.entries` only iterates keys the object itself owns.
- **API-01:** the `useResolvedSidebarNav` signature change is additive.
- **UX-03:** no shell was replaced.
- **FEAT-04:** no edits under `components/ui/*`.
- **Slice registration:** the store is registered the same way as the `hypernative` and `gtf` slices.

### Minor, outside the rules

- `apps/web/src/features/feature-flags/components/FeatureFlagRow.tsx:85`: `tabIndex={isOverridden ? undefined : -1}` sits inside an `{isOverridden && ...}` block, so the `-1` case can never happen.
- `apps/web/src/features/spaces/components/Sidebar/variants/SafeSidebarContent/SafeSidebarContent.tsx:116` checks `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_IS_PRODUCTION` directly instead of using `IS_PRODUCTION` from `@/config/constants`. Unlike the two other files, it has no build-time pruning reason for doing so.
